chronicle.journalHint: Choose a date to open its chronicle. Missing chronicles do not mean inactive days. Monthly totals and the existing AI story are shown here separately.
chronicle.loadError: Could not load the chronicle. Your local note draft has been kept.
chronicle.timelineError: Could not load the day's timeline.
chronicle.accuracy: AI summaries may be inaccurate or omit context. Check the recorded sources; this is not a health assessment or proof of cause and effect.
chronicle.generationHint: Generate uses allowed facts and the configured default AI, which may be paid. An existing chronicle is returned from cache, not rewritten. No allowed facts means no new chronicle.
chronicle.generated: Chronicle ready (an existing chronicle may have been reused).
chronicle.noFacts: No allowed facts to generate a chronicle. Your personal note is unchanged.
chronicle.actionError: The change could not be completed. Your local note draft has been kept; check your connection and AI settings, then try again.
chronicle.confirmDelete: Delete the chronicle and personal note for {{day}}? This cannot be undone. Unsaved edits for this date will also be discarded.
chronicle.noteHint: Your own words, separate from the generated summary. Save explicitly. Unsaved drafts stay while switching dates here, but not when leaving this page.
chronicle.saved: Note saved. Any newer edits still need saving.
chronicle.nightlyHint: Off by default and separate from manual generation. When enabled, the server checks hourly after 03:00 in your configured timezone and attempts yesterday's chronicle once per day. This is not a full NightButler service.
chronicle.privacy: Generation respects module access in AI privacy settings. The configured default AI may incur charges. Personal notes remain separate from generated text.
chronicle.settingsError: Could not load or save nightly settings. No change has been confirmed.

story.title: The story by the AI
story.nothing: Nothing to tell about this period yet.
story.error: The AI could not write it: check the AI connection in Settings.

mood.title: What goes with a good day
mood.hint: The numbers of every section on the days of a good mood (4–5 in the diary) against the days of a bad one (1–2). It shows what goes together, not what causes what.
mood.few: Too few days with a mood to compare: {{good}} good and {{bad}} bad. At least three of each are needed — mark the mood in the diary.
mood.of: {{good}} good days against {{bad}} bad ones — the average of a day:
mood.same: Nothing differs noticeably between good and bad days.

digital.hint: Filter links involving desktop or browser telemetry, then select a pair in the matrix or list to plot its observed days. Missing measurements are unknown, not zero. These are digital observations, not biometrics or productivity scores.
digital.empty: No comparable pairs for this selection yet. Try another metric or a longer period.

links.caution: Links show what goes together and what comes before what — not what causes what. A third thing (a busy week, an illness) can be behind both. The seasons are taken away (each day is compared with the weeks around it, so “more games and warmer in summer” is not a link), and the chance of an accident is corrected for the number of pairs and for the days' own trends.
links.failed: Could not count the links. Please try later.
links.none: No strong links yet among {{metrics}} daily numbers. They need weeks of data: mark the mood in the diary, keep the tracker on, and come back in a while.
links.thenMore: After a day of more {{a}}, more {{b}} the next day
links.thenLess: After a day of more {{a}}, less {{b}} the next day
links.leadsHint: It tells about the next day even with that day's own yesterday held fixed (Granger's idea): a hint of the order, still not proof of a cause.

top.title: The strongest links
top.hint: {{links}} strong links among {{metrics}} daily numbers. A click shows the pair day by day.

graph.title: The map of links
graph.hint: A line — the same day, an arrow — to the next day; the theme's colour — together, red — against. A click on a number explains it below.

pair.title: A pair day by day
pair.hintSame: Each point is a day. The line is how the two change together from day to day, the seasons taken away.
pair.hintNext: Each point is a day: across — that day, up — the next one. The line is how the two change together from day to day, the seasons taken away.

regression.title: What predicts a number
regression.hint: A regression: the numbers most linked to it together, each with the others held fixed.
regression.explained: Together they explain {{share}} of its change from day to day ({{days}} days).
regression.legend: Bars: the change of the number, in its usual spreads, for one usual spread of the other, the rest held fixed. Faded — could be an accident (p ≥ 5%).
regression.few: Not enough days with this number and the numbers linked to it to fit a regression.

matrix.title: All pairs
matrix.hintSame: Every pair of the same day; a dot marks a strong link. A click shows the pair.
matrix.hintNext: A row's day against the column's next day; a dot marks a strong link.

beforeAfter.title: Before and after
beforeAfter.hint: How your days changed at a date of Health (a diagnosis, a medication) or an event of Psychology: the weeks before against the weeks after.
beforeAfter.wait: {{days}} days have passed since the date; at least 7 are needed to compare — come back in {{left}} days.
beforeAfter.none: Nothing changed beyond what ordinary weeks do.
beforeAfter.caution: An observation from your own data, not a medical judgement, and not proof of a cause: a change is marked when ordinary dates of your history rarely show one as large. It may be worth showing to your doctor.
beforeAfter.noHistory: Too little history around this date to tell a change from the usual: try shorter windows, or come back later.

forecast.title: Today's mood, forecast
forecast.hint: From yesterday's numbers of every section, by a model of your own days
forecast.quality: Learned from {{days}} days; on the latest ones it missed by {{error}} on average, "like the last week" by {{baseline}}. What weighs most:
forecast.few: Needs at least 40 days with a mood in the diary — there are {{days}} so far.
forecast.notBetter: Your days do not tell yet more than "like the last week": no forecast to trust.
